$comment: Hand-checked facts for each Trust Task type. The build finds the types themselves by scanning the code for ourSpec("..."); a type found in code without an entry here still gets a page, built from its doc comment, and the build prints a warning. payloadType/responseType name a declaration the build extracts from payloadFile/responseFile, so the shape shown is the code's.

settle/payment/request.purpose: The payee sends an invoice to the payer. It carries the price, the purpose, a new payment key bound to the payee's DID, and the payee's credentials. The payer checks the key binding and the credentials and records the invoice. If the invoice answers one of its own checkouts, the payer then proposes terms without a click.
settle/payment/request.note: The payee also sends it in reply to settle/checkout/start. Then the payload has link, checkout and conditions set.

settle/payment/terms/propose.purpose: The payer sends the full terms document with its own signed acceptance. The payee checks the terms against its invoice and its limits: price, purpose, token, arbiter, fee, threshold, reclaim deadline, payment-link conditions and the payer's key binding. If everything checks out, it accepts.
settle/payment/terms/propose.note: The design says either side may propose. In the code only the payer does.

settle/payment/terms/accept.purpose: The payee returns the agreed terms with its own signed acceptance. The payer checks that the terms are the ones it proposed and that the payee signed them. It then opens the escrow through the processor.
settle/payment/terms/accept.note: The design says the payload is the terms with both proofs. The code sends the terms and the payee's acceptance only.

settle/escrow/opened.purpose: After the escrow opens on-chain, the payer announces it with the terms, both acceptances, the escrow address and the opening transaction signature. The payee checks the escrow on-chain, field by field. The attester and the arbiter accept it only if it comes from the payer, carries both acceptances and matches the chain. The processor records it in its transparency log.
settle/escrow/opened.to: payee's party, attester, arbiter and processor
settle/escrow/opened.note: The design says the payer or the processor sends it. In the code only the payer does.

settle/escrow/attest.purpose: The attester named in the terms sends a signed claim that the work is complete or not complete, with an optional note. The payer, the payee and the arbiter verify it and record it as input to their release policies.
settle/escrow/attest.to: payer's party, payee's party and arbiter
settle/escrow/attest.note: The attester can be the payer, with the link option payer-confirms. The design mentions photos sealed to the parties; the code carries only an optional note.

settle/escrow/sign.purpose: A party sends its signature over an escrow outcome (how much of the price goes to the payee), with the evidence the outcome rests on. The processor collects these and submits the on-chain resolve once enough distinct allowed keys sign the same outcome. When the payee sends one to the payer, it asks for a release or a refund, which the payer checks against its policy.
settle/escrow/sign.to: processor, and the payer's party when the payee asks for a release or refund
settle/escrow/sign.note: The arbiter's outcome signature travels inside settle/arbiter/ruling instead. The design's escrow/release/request type is not separate in the code: the payee's escrow/sign to the payer takes its place.

settle/escrow/dispute.purpose: The payer or the payee sends a signed dispute with a reason. The arbiter records it and signs a hold, so the payer can't reclaim before a ruling. The other party records it, and the processor logs it by role and hash.
settle/escrow/dispute.to: arbiter, the other party and processor
settle/escrow/dispute.note: The design lists the arbiter and the other party. The code also sends it to the processor.

settle/arbiter/ruling.purpose: The arbiter sends its signed ruling on a disputed payment, with the evidence it relied on and its own outcome signature. Each party runs its policy on the ruling and, if the policy allows, signs the same outcome. The processor logs the ruling and counts the arbiter's signature toward the threshold.
settle/arbiter/ruling.to: payer's party, payee's party and processor

settle/escrow/settled.purpose: After it submits the resolve transaction, the processor tells everyone the escrow settled, with the transaction signature, the payee's share and the evidence hash. Each party confirms the settlement against the chain. The payee then sends the payer a receipt.
settle/escrow/settled.to: payer's party, payee's party and arbiter

settle/escrow/hold.purpose: On a dispute, the arbiter signs a hold that pushes back the escrow's reclaim deadline, so the payer can't wait out the deadline before a ruling. The processor checks the arbiter's signature against the escrow's arbiter key and submits the hold on-chain.
settle/escrow/hold.designSection: 16. Security review and escrow program v2 (2026-11-06)
settle/escrow/hold.note: Added by the security review. The table in design section 7 doesn't list it.

settle/payment/receipt.purpose: After settlement, the payee sends the payer a signed receipt credential (SettlePaymentReceipt). It ties together the terms hash, the escrow address, the settlement transaction, the amount paid and the purpose. The payer verifies it and keeps it.

settle/processor/submit.purpose: A party sends the processor a partly signed transaction: an escrow open, reclaim or claim. The processor checks that it holds one Settle instruction that uses the processor's key only for fees and rent, and, for an open, that it matches terms both parties signed. Then it co-signs as fee payer and submits it.
settle/processor/submit.note: Design section 7 says every Settle task is one-way. This one is request/response. A refusal comes back as { ok: false, error }.

settle/processor/log.purpose: Anyone can ask the processor for its transparency log. The reply holds every entry (openings, signatures, disputes, rulings, holds and settlements, recorded as roles and hashes) and the processor's signed head.
settle/processor/log.note: The demo and tests send it. The web app reads the same log over HTTP at /api/log.

settle/checkout/start.purpose: A payer who opens a payment link sends the link back to its issuer and asks for an invoice under the link's conditions. The payee checks that the link is its own, unchanged and not archived, then sends a settle/payment/request with those conditions.
settle/checkout/start.payloadInline: { link: PaymentLink; checkout: string; name?: string }
settle/checkout/start.designSection: 17. The app: platform, parties, payment links (2026-11-06)

todo/join.purpose: A device holding an invitation asks the inviting admin to join the list, with the invitation code, the list's DID and a display name. The admin checks the code, adds the member to a newly signed roster and issues a membership credential, or refuses.
todo/join.payloadInline: { code: string; list: string; name: string }

todo/welcome.purpose: The admin admits a joiner. It sends the list's name, the joiner's membership credential and the current signed roster. The joiner verifies all three and replies with todo/ack. The list's history follows as todo/sync pages.
todo/welcome.payloadInline: { listName: string; membership: Credential; roster: RosterDoc }

todo/join-refused.purpose: The admin tells a joiner why it won't admit them: the invitation is unknown, used or expired, the joiner is already a member, or this device doesn't run the list. The joiner records the reason against its pending join.

todo/ack.purpose: A new member sends the admin a signed acknowledgement credential (TodoListMembershipAcknowledgement) after accepting the welcome. The admin verifies it and records that the member acknowledged.

todo/op.purpose: A member who adds, edits, checks, unchecks or deletes an item sends the signed operation, with their membership credential, to every other current member. Each device checks it against the roster, the credential and the policy before applying it.

todo/roster.purpose: The admin sends the list's newly signed roster after someone joins or is removed. A device adopts a roster only if the list's key signed it, its version is higher, and it keeps every earlier removal.
todo/roster.to: every current member's device, and once to a member just removed

todo/sync-request.purpose: On start and on reconnect, a device asks one other current member (a different one each time) for everything it holds for a list. The receiver answers with todo/sync pages if the requester is a current member.
todo/sync-request.note: The answer is a separate one-way todo/sync, not a response.

todo/sync.purpose: A device sends one page of a list's history: the current signed roster, up to 100 operations, and the membership credentials those operations need. The receiver adopts the roster as it would any roster and checks each operation as if it had arrived on its own.

todo/leave.purpose: A member who isn't the admin tells the list's admins they are leaving. The admin's device removes them and sends a newly signed roster.

mandates/issue.purpose: A delegator sends its delegate a new mandate, with the chain of mandates above it. The receiver checks that the sender issued the mandate and that the whole chain verifies and only narrows. With a status resolver, it checks the chain's status lists too.
mandates/issue.from: delegator (a principal, or an agent delegating to a sub-agent)

mandates/revoked.purpose: A delegator tells its delegate that a mandate was revoked, with the mandate's id and the delegator's newly signed status list. The receiver checks the sender signed the list, then checks its own mandate against it.

mandates/approval/request.purpose: A delegate asks an approver to allow one action its mandate chain doesn't allow by itself. The request carries the action, its hash, the chain, the decision and, optionally, the delegate's own justification. The receiver checks that the action matches its hash and that the chain verifies for the sender.
mandates/approval/request.note: The answer is a separate one-way mandates/approval/grant or mandates/approval/deny.

mandates/approval/grant.purpose: The approver returns a signed approval for a pending request. The receiver checks that the sender signed it over the action's hash, then passes it to the decision.

mandates/approval/deny.purpose: The approver tells the delegate it refused a pending request, with an optional reason.

trail/witness/submit.purpose: A log's controller sends a witness KEL events or trail messages to witness. The witness verifies each one, keeps the first version it sees at each position, and returns receipts. If it refuses, it says why, and on duplicity it returns the version it saw first.
trail/witness/submit.note: The same operation is also served over HTTP (witnessHttpHandler).

trail/witness/receipts.purpose: A log's controller passes each witness the receipts the other witnesses signed, so every witness ends up holding every receipt. The witness stores them and replies with an empty object.

trail/query.purpose: A watcher or verifier asks a witness for a log's messages and receipts, optionally for a range of sequence numbers. The witness returns them as a CESR text stream.
trail/query.payloadInline: { logId: Qb64; from?: number; to?: number }
trail/query.note: Qb64 is a string: a CESR primitive in its text form.

trail/head.purpose: A watcher or verifier asks a witness for the head of a log: the latest receipt that witness signed. Watchers compare heads to catch forks and truncated bundles.

trail/disclose.purpose: A log's controller sends a reader a bundle: the KEL, the chosen trails with the bodies picked for this reader, and the DID bindings. The reader verifies the bundle and reviews the entries, and replies with an empty object.

trail/duplicity.purpose: Whoever catches duplicity sends the evidence to someone who relies on the log: two conflicting signed versions at the same position, from the controller or from a witness. The evidence proves itself against the controller's KEL. The receiver replies with an empty object.
trail/duplicity.from: whoever caught it (a watcher, controller or verifier)
trail/duplicity.to: a party that relies on the log

anon-membership/enroll.purpose: A member's wallet, from the member's own DID, sends a group's issuer a commitment to its secret for that group, optionally with a credential. The issuer's admit() decides whether that DID may join; if so, the issuer appends the commitment as a leaf in the group's tree. It answers with the leaf's index, the first epoch whose root will hold it, and the leaf, which the wallet checks.
anon-membership/enroll.note: Refusals: unknownGroup, badRequest (the commitment isn't a field element) and notAdmitted. The design's table leaves out the optional credential and the leaf in the response.
